messages:
Taylor: hey folks, Taylor here  day 1! Quick sanity check: where do I post  laptop/setup issues, noisy CI/build failures, product feature ideas, and small UX asks? Also, a bunch of bots DM'd me when I joined. How do I mute those without losing pages?

Maya: welcome! short map: laptop/setup -> #help (attach screenshot + OS), noisy CI -> mute #build-failures and rely on paging for real outages, prod ideas -> #product-feedback (or the squad channel if it's specific), UX -> #design or DM a designer for quick Qs.

Taylor: got it. what's the preferred format for asking setup stuff so it's easy to triage?

Rox: one-line problem + one-line context + command/log snippet. example: "docker permission denied on macOS 13.2 when running `rwi-setup`". Paste only the relevant 1-2 lines of error. That helps us route quickly.

infra-bot: Hello Taylor! To finish onboarding run:

```
$ rwi-setup --full
$ rwi-auth login --machine
```

Reply "done" when complete.

Taylor: ran it, hit "permission denied: /var/run/docker.sock". who should I ping?

Maya: ping @Rox or open a post in #help and tag "infra". Include the error and your hostname. If it's blocking you, put [URGENT] at the start of the message.

Taylor: nice. about bots: I got DMs from deploy-bot, ci-bot, and kitty-bot (lol). I want deploy/ops pages to reach me but not CI noise.

Rox: go to Apps -> find the bot -> click "Notifications" -> choose "Mute" or uncheck direct messages. For channel noise, click the bell on the channel header and set notifications to "Mentions & keywords". Add "@oncall" to your notification keywords so pages still break through.

eng: also, add paging keywords for urgent alerts like "SEV" or "P0" if you want redundancy. We recommend keeping DND off for nights if you're oncall.

Taylor: thanks. one more: when is it okay to use @channel / @here / @team? timezone-conscious folks here.

Rox: rules of thumb: @channel for company/team-wide announcements only and preferably scheduled, @here for time-sensitive asks (use sparingly), @team (user groups) only after checking with the team lead. If in doubt, DM a lead or post in the thread and ask for async replies.

Maya: quick etiquette: 1) use threads for follow ups in busy channels, 2) add one-line summary + link to PR/issue, 3) use reactions for ACKs instead of "thanks" replies, 4) prefix posts with [Help]/[FYI]/[Decision] for clarity/search.

kitty-bot: purr! Newbie tip: try `rwi-setup --quiet` for minimal bot output. :cat_tech: 

Taylor: perfect. where should I drop my intro post? #introductions or my team channel?

Rox: post a short intro in #introductions (name, role, timezone, 1 fun thing). In your team channel add what you're starting on this week so people know who to ping.

Taylor: awesome, posting now. thanks all :raised_hands:
